notes: The bridge between ReSharper's key namespace and Skala's, in the one direction that still exists. Skala's own keys are `skala_*`; this file records the spelling(s) the Rider export (`editor_config_template`) writes for each of them. It is the only place in the option registry that names another tool's keys.

⚠ Provenance, not ingestion. Nothing here is indexed by `OptionRegistry.TryResolve`, so a `resharper_*` key in a user's .editorconfig is still an unknown key (SK9001). Three consumers read it as an artefact: `CanonicalEditorConfig.Compose`, which translates the export into the payload `skala config sync` ships; `OracleRunner`, which has to speak this namespace to `jb cleanupcode` because that is the only namespace it understands; and `EditorConfigIngestionTests`.

⚠ The mapping is recorded, not computed. `skala_x` is `resharper_x` for some keys and `resharper_csharp_x` for others, and most keys carry both plus unprefixed forms, so no rule derives it. Delete an entry and the key-flip sweep reports that option INERT — silently, because the oracle ignores a key it cannot read — and the canonical payload loses the line.

⚠ Order within each array is significance order, most specific first, and is load-bearing twice: `CanonicalEditorConfig.Translate` uses the index as the specificity rank when the export sets one option under two spellings in one section, and `ExportSpellings.ForOracle` hands element 0 to the oracle. Handing the oracle a generic spelling whose specific spelling the export also sets would leave the export's value in force and measure nothing.
Every option in options.json has an entry here and every entry names an option that exists; the generator fails the build (SKG006, SKG007) if either stops being true.

`unmapped` is the other half: foreign keys that options.json's measurements name but that Skala carries no option for. They are here so that a measurement stays reproducible — a reader who wants to repeat a negative control needs the exact spelling — without options.json holding it. ⚠ Not all of them are export keys: `braces_for_ifelse` and `remove_this_qualifier` are the reference formatter's settings, verified absent from `editor_config_template` on 2026-09-04; the other three the export does write.

unmapped.resharper_braces_for_ifelse: csharp_prefer_braces' negative control. Flat at required, not_required and required_for_multiline under both oracle profiles, which is what shows neither profile performs brace insertion at all. ⚠ Not written by the export.
unmapped.resharper_csharp_align_multiline_argumen: Named by skala_allow_far_alignment's measurement. The export sets it false at editor_config_template:262; the probe that overturned the OfInert registration set it true.
unmapped.resharper_new_line_before_enumerators: The key that actually chops an enum under this export (editor_config_template:413, = true). It is what masks skala_wrap_enum_declaration and skala_max_enum_members_on_line.
unmapped.resharper_parentheses_non_obvious_operat: Shift and the bitwise family, which dotnet_style_parentheses_in_arithmetic_binary_operators does not govern (editor_config_template:426).
unmapped.resharper_remove_this_qualifier: Named by dotnet_style_qualification_for_field: the key the oracle does NOT read for `this.` (SK-DIV-0070). ⚠ Not written by the export.
